requirements.requirement: Rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily through an operational scheduling mechanism.
requirements.summary: The installed rule specifies daily rotation, logrotate parses it as a one-day interval, and logrotate.timer was enabled and active both before and after the node restart.

The installed and persisted rule specifies rotate 7 and compress. A forced rotation directly produced a readable, valid app.log.1.gz containing the prior log data, and logrotate parsed the policy as seven rotations.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation.
requirements.summary: A descriptor opened before the forced rotation successfully wrote a post-rotation record to the live app.log, while preceding content appeared in the compressed archive. The live log also remained writable after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also strong: a healthy pre-restart configuration and timer were captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, the boot ID changed from d052eb57-c81d-4309-ae7f-bce362073ff9 to 557d0837-6abe-4e52-9f0f-4e9a367cbc65, and the configuration, timer, archived data, and live-log writability were verified after recovery. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Seven-generation retention was verified through the installed and parsed policy rather than by creating eight successive rotations and observing eviction.
The daily scheduler was shown enabled and active, but evidence did not wait for a naturally elapsed daily run; functional rotation itself was demonstrated with a bounded forced run.
Two task-related temporary files remained under /tmp after completion.

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unrelated state-changing experiments were identified. Installing the rule, performing a bounded forced rotation and write-continuity test, rebooting under the mandatory protocol, and making a post-reboot test write all directly supported implementation or verification. However, the executor left two task-related temporary artifacts behind: /tmp/inventory-logrotate.conf from configuration staging and /tmp/inventory-logrotate.state from the isolated rotation test. These were low-risk but abandoned rather than cleaned up. No failed services, new network exposure, or package-health damage was observed after execution.
